A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DAM research and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C. Additions and relocated material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-merging experiments, backdoor evaluations, mask ablations, and supplementary results across six image-classification datasets and two CLIP backbones.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and additionally reports runtime measurements and a domain-source experiment in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The DAM objective, perturbation recovery, mask sampling, rescaling, and optimization procedure are retained. Appendix B.1 already specifies the shared M1 = M2 implementation in v1; combining two pseudocode lines in v2 does not change the algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same six image-classification datasets and attack families. The added domain-source study reuses this coverage and changes the compromised-checkpoint mixture, without introducing new data domains or task requirements.

E2.justification: All corresponding comparisons retain their merging and defense baselines, including WAG/LoRA-as-an-Attack and BadMerging evaluations. The new studies use existing comparators; newly discussed routing, inversion, and continual-learning methods are not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix C.4 introduces a runtime comparison using six checkpoints, a Tesla V100 with 32 GB memory, AdamW, and batch size 16. C.5 adds a reported DTD-only compromise condition, although Table 15 inconsistently labels SVHN as backdoored. Existing evaluation metrics and attack-construction settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds computational-efficiency measurements and a domain-source analysis examining backdoor dilution and transfer when DTD alone is reportedly compromised. Existing mask ablations, attack-type tests, and compromised-model-count studies are retained. Tables 13–14 redisplay existing evidence rather than introduce additional analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or variability estimates. The added tables continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in retained result tables match. New Table 8 reports total times of 35 minutes for DAM versus 44, 47, and 49 for ANP, AWM, and SAU. New Table 15 reports DAM average ACC/ASR of 86.77/23.99. These are additional measurements, not improvements over corresponding v1 results.

T1.justification: Equation 2 introduces an explicit weight omega on the safety term, generalizing the previously unweighted performance–safety criterion. DAM's objective, Theorem 1, its proof, and the convergence analysis remain unchanged; the proof moves into Appendix B.3.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: identifying backdoor succession and transfer, proposing DAM, and improving the accuracy–security trade-off. The headline claim of reducing ASR by 2–10 percentage points while sacrificing about 1% accuracy is unchanged.

C2.justification: Sections 2.2–2.3 and new Appendix B.5 substantially expand the threat and mechanism explanations: attacker ignorance of other checkpoints and merging algorithms, transfer through task-general parameters, and reliance on a clean, protected pretrained model. Appendix C.5 additionally interprets domain-related backdoor dilution and residual transfer, extending the earlier mask-trade-off discussion.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a promised future release with a code/model access link. Appendix C.4 newly supplies hardware, optimizer, batch-size, and runtime information for its efficiency experiment. Existing mask implementation details and attack-construction hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: Appendix A.1 adds routing-based merging literature. New Appendix B.4 substantially expands positioning against trigger inversion, fine-tuning defenses, and continual learning, distinguishing their data requirements and single-model optimization from DAM's merging setting. Supporting additions include Sun and Kolter, Huang et al., and Abbasi et al.

P1.justification: Most core prose is retained. v2 separates attack/defense settings into Section 2.2, moves the proof into the appendix, adds discussion and experimental subsections, and makes localized explanatory edits. Author information, publication headers, and acknowledgments also change.

P2.justification: The eight figures and existing table designs are retained with placement and sizing adjustments. The mixed-attack table moves from main-text Table 4 to appendix Table 9. Four tables are added: runtime and domain results, plus Tables 13–14 reproducing SVHN and EuroSAT columns from Table 2.

improvement.justification: v2 provides quantitative support for the computational-cost claim, clearer threat and trust assumptions, and code/model access instructions while preserving the original evidence. These gains are tempered by inconsistencies in the added domain analysis: Table 15's SVHN header conflicts with the stated setup, and C.5 attributes Concrete AM results to AdaMerging. The net improvement is useful but limited.
